The role of ascorbate in iron absorption
Inorganic dietary iron is absorbed as Fe2þ, and not as Fe3þ; ascorbic acid in the intestinal lumen not only maintains iron in the
reduced state but also chelates it, increasing absorption considerably. A dose of 25 mg of vitamin C taken together with a meal
increases the absorption of iron approximately 65%, whereas a 1 g dose gives a ninefold increase. This is an effect of ascorbic
acid present together with the test meal
